what: The heuristic precomputes semantic loc/visited fact mappings, numeric resource IDs, customer demands, directed direct-visit costs, directed via-depot costs, depot return costs, and a directed greedy base tour. Travel costs are extracted primarily from grounded visit, visit-via-depot, and return-to-depot operators. For each state it reads the current location, visited set, load, vehicles used, capacity, and fleet limit; checks aggregate fleet-capacity feasibility; chooses a state-dependent first customer; filters and rotates the precomputed tour over the actual unvisited set; simulates direct visits and via-depot reloads; adds the final depot return; and adds explicit capacity-pressure and fleet-pressure components.
why: The representative instances contain tens of customers, so the implementation avoids per-state matrix construction and sorting, using an O(n) filtered completion over precomputed task structure. Their heterogeneous demands and capacity-limited routes motivate using remaining demand, current load, and residual capacity both for dead-end detection and reload estimation. The small fixed fleet and frequent need for multiple depot-separated routes motivate explicit modeling of vehicles used and visit-via-depot transitions rather than a purely geometric tour. The dense explicit metric travel-cost matrices motivate reconstructing directed costs from grounded operators and retaining directionality. This is more informative than unvisited count because it responds to customer identities, route geometry, load, and location; more informative than a sum of depot distances because it includes customer-to-customer arcs and the current route endpoint; and more reliable than a purely geometric estimate because it detects fleet-capacity dead ends and prices forced depot reloads.
instance_patterns: Single-depot CVRP with a mandatory final return to the depot
Tens of customers, making cheap O(n) state evaluation preferable
Small fleet with capacity-induced visit-via-depot route changes
Heterogeneous customer demands relative to vehicle capacity
Dense explicit pairwise travel costs that are symmetric in examples but treated as directed
Goals require every customer visited and the vehicle located at the depot
design: Geometric routing estimate via a state-anchored, filtered directed greedy tour
Capacity/resource bound using remaining demand, residual load capacity, and remaining fleet capacity
Precomputed tour positions and reusable evaluation scratch buffers
complexity: O(n) per state after O(n^2) task-dependent preprocessing, where n is the number of customers.
fallbacks: Grounded routing operators are the primary cost source. Missing direct travel arcs are next recovered from simple travel-cost PNEs when available. Still-missing customer arcs are filled only when a directed return-to-depot leg and depot-to-customer leg provide a valid via-depot path. Construction fails with a clear HeuristicBuildError if directed depot legs, demands, resource variables, or a usable routing matrix cannot be recovered.
known_limitations: The filtered base tour is a fast greedy approximation and may poorly represent the best completion for irregular customer subsets, despite being re-anchored from the current state.
The aggregate fleet-capacity test does not solve bin packing, so it cannot detect every capacity infeasibility caused by indivisible demands.
The capacity and fleet-pressure weights are intentionally non-admissible guidance terms and may overestimate remaining routing cost.
